_comment: Budgets, conventions and thresholds per kind of animated model. A game's manifest may override any value or add profiles under "profiles"; one asset's own values (above all its "animations" spec and "required" names) go under its entry's "overrides". Distances are fractions of the model's size (the largest side of its bounds at rest) unless they say seconds, degrees or a count, so one number suits a hero and a seven-unit boss.

default._comment: Anything else. No ground plane is assumed; budgets are loose.
default._engine_fps: The engine advances animations once a tick, 60 times a second, and poses the model at that time.
default._ground: true: the model stands on y = 0 (origin at its base), so sinking through it is checked in every animation not declared "grounded": false.
default._max_skinned_parts: The engine's own limit: it animates 16 skinned parts of an entity and draws the rest unposed.
default._pop: A pop is a followed point that, in one frame, either jumps out and straight back by more than pop_size_fraction (pop_ratio times further than in the calmer frame beside the pair and half that against the busier one), or leaps and stays by more than leap_size_fraction (pop_ratio times further than in the frames on either side); and in both cases pop_ratio times what is usual for it within pop_neighbourhood_seconds. An eased snap over three frames is not one.
default._handover: How far apart two poses may be where one animation hands over to another: cut_size_fraction when the game cuts, fade_size_fraction when it cross-fades (entity:play's third argument), which hides a small mismatch but not a different stance.
default._deform_vertex_poses: The mesh is skinned at every frame of an animation up to this many vertices times frames; beyond it, at evenly spaced frames.
default._views: How the review sheet looks at the model, as [yaw, pitch] in degrees: yaw 0 faces its front (+Z), 90 its left side, 270 its right. game_view is the side the game's camera shows; ground_view is level with the ground.

character._comment: A rigged figure about as tall as the heroes, standing on the ground: idle, walk, attack, hit, die and the like.

boss._comment: A large rigged creature or machine with many animations, standing on the ground.

prop._comment: A prop whose nodes move: a door, a wheel, a lever, a chest lid. Usually one or two short animations.

set_piece._comment: A large one-off that moves by itself: a floating crystal, a siege engine, a windmill. Long, slow loops.
